reviewer: Independent parable source and pixel review
scope: Two exact generated thief-at-night originals reviewed at full original image detail; source fit, anatomy, architecture, lighting, and hand-to-bolt contact.
globalConditions: Technical and source review does not constitute owner approval.
Use these as illustrations of Jesus's hypothetical comparison, not as a recorded burglary or a portrayal of Christ.

entries.alt: Moonlight falls on a stone house, with warm light shining around its wooden door and shuttered window.
entries.caption: Warm light shines around the door of a quiet house beneath the night sky. Jesus asks His listeners to consider how a homeowner would keep watch if he knew when a thief would come.
findings: The exterior supplies a distinct nighttime establishing moment; no person, sleeping household, thief, or attempted entry is visible.

Stone and plaster walls, wooden door and shutters, terrace steps, earthenware, and contrasting moonlight and indoor light are visually coherent. These are permissible illustrative details, not an exact architectural reconstruction.
The interior light source is not visible; caption describes light rather than claiming a visible lamp. Matthew 24:43 presents a hypothetical comparison, not a recorded burglary.
conditions: Use the supplied actual alt and source-grounded caption; retain the hypothetical narrative framing.

entries.alt: A man rests a hand on a wooden door bolt beside a burning oil lamp and a shuttered window.
entries.caption: The householder rests a hand on the wooden bolt while an oil lamp burns beside him. Jesus uses the watchful homeowner to teach the value of being ready before an unexpected arrival.
findings: The visible hand rests naturally on the top and front of the horizontal bolt, with plausible finger contact and no apparent extra digits. Bolt, brackets, door, and adjoining frame form a coherent arrangement.
The bolt appears seated; a checking or watchful gesture is supported, but active sliding or successful exclusion of an intruder is not established.
Face, eye direction toward the window, draped clothing, lamp flame, ledge, and nighttime illumination appear photographically coherent. The man is an ordinary fictional householder, not Christ.
Luke 12:39 is a hypothetical homeowner comparison; readiness is the teaching, not fear or a claim that a burglary was recorded. No intruder is visible.
conditions: Use the supplied actual alt and source-grounded caption; retain the hypothetical narrative framing.
